Avogadro guide · Minecraft 1.12.2 / Cleanroom

Definition and recipe reference

Compact tables for every authoring field, path, edit operation, and source layer. Use the guides for worked examples and the API pages for signatures.

Example language Your choice applies across the guides.

File locations and precedence

File locations and precedence
OrderSourcePath / effect
1Mod common resourcesdata/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
2Retained Java registrationsAvogadroApi.owner(...)
3Instance common JSONconfig/avogadro/server/data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
4World JSON<world>/avogadro/data/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json
5GroovyScriptVirtualized registration layer
Client overlay 1Client assets/resourcesassets/<namespace>/molecules/<path>.json in mods, packs, server pack, then config/avogadro/resources/assets
Client overlay 2Local JSONconfig/avogadro/molecules/<path>.json → avogadro:<path>

Later valid same-ID definitions win. A rejected override can leave an earlier valid definition in place. Clients receive the common server snapshot before their local overlays. No vanilla 1.12 datapack engine is involved; a world datapacks folder is not an Avogadro source. Organize IDs with lowercase descriptive paths such as organic/ethanol.

Molecule fields

Molecule fields
FieldType / defaultMeaning
nameStringOptional display name, 1–256 characters
formulaStringOptional ordinary-digit formula; otherwise derived from atoms. Generated-item composition must agree
smilesStringConnectivity plus schematic layout; adds implicit H according to supported valence rules
atomsArrayEvery explicit atom: e, x, y, z; optional nuclear data
bondsArray[from,to] or [from,to,type]; indices start at 0. Missing means distance inference; [] disables it
structureObjectFragment recipe / assembly. Cannot coexist with copy, atoms, bonds, or smiles
copyString IDCopy a supplied definition; cycles/missing targets fail. Inherit missing fields; associations union
editsArrayOrdered edits after geometry/copy resolution
materializeBooleanRequired when editing a crystal/polymer preview into a finite result
polymerObjectLinear chain recipe with explicit caps
polymer_networkObjectParameterized network recipe, seed, algorithm version
crystalObjectCell lengths, angles, optional origin
items / fluidsSelector arraysRegistry IDs, item metadata, partial NBT requirements
item_tags / fluid_tagsString arraysAvogadro association dictionary IDs
materialsString arrayOptional supported legacy GregTech material IDs
match_containersBoolean; trueAllow contained-fluid associations
generate_itemBoolean; falseExpose a sample through the shared molecule item, not a new registry item
elementsObjectPer-symbol neutral nuclear/shell defaults
atom_configurationsObjectPer-index atomic overrides; not flattened network overrides
componentsArrayReferences for inspection; do not add geometry
inspectionObjectString-valued inspection metadata and presentation classification
diagram / tooltipLegacy valuesAccepted but ignored; use current presentation settings
Tip Choose one geometry source. For old mixed definitions, copy wins over atoms and atoms wins over SMILES, but new content should avoid mixing them. Unsupported top-level and atom/structure fields are rejected. IDs come from file paths; do not add an id field. Each resource file is limited to 256 KiB.

Supported SMILES and bonds

Supported SMILES and bonds
ChemicalSMILESFormula
WaterOH2O
MethaneCCH4
EthanolCCOC2H6O
AcetoneCC(=O)CC3H6O
Benzenec1ccccc1C6H6
Acetic acidCC(=O)OC2H4O2
Carbon dioxideO=C=OCO2

Supported: branches, disconnected pieces, digit/%nn ring closures, common organic/aromatic and bracket atoms, and bond symbols - = # : / \. Chirality and slash markers are not stereochemical geometry instructions. Bracket isotope/charge syntax does not supply examiner nuclear data. Use explicit atomic configurations for that.

Supported SMILES and bonds
Bond inputType
Omitted third entry / SINGLE / 1 / -Single
DOUBLE / 2 / =Double
TRIPLE / 3 / #Triple
QUADRUPLE / 4Quadruple

All JSON edit operations

All JSON edit operations
opRequired fieldsEffect
replaceAtomindex, eChange element; clear old atom configuration if changed
moveAtomindex, x, y, zMove one atom
atome, x, y, zAppend an atom
setBondfrom, to; optional typeCreate/replace a bond
removeBondfrom, toRemove an edge
removeAtomsindices arrayResolve all current indices, then delete and remap
appendinstance, structureAppend a named fragment
connectfrom, to attachment paths; optional typeConnect named atoms
attachmentname, indexAdd an attachment
removeAttachmentnameRemove a name
atomConfigurationindex, nuclearAssign atomic data
clearAtomConfigurationindexRemove atomic data
randomLinkCapacityindex, capacityAssign additional random-link capacity

At most 64 edit operations. Syntax validates immediately; geometry-dependent references validate against the resolved copy source. Each operation sees indices after previous operations.

Structure recipes and assembly JSON

Structure recipes and assembly JSON
ShapeFields / use
Base fragmentatoms (optional nuclear data per atom), bonds, attachments, random_link_capacities; optional cell with vectors and links
Ordered operationstranslate, rotate, scale, affine, repeat, append, instances, wrapCylinder; see StructureFragment and its serialized recipe
Finite assemblystructure: {assembly: {nodes: […], links: […], random_links: […]}}
Fragment nodename, kind="fragment", structure, optional transform
Group nodename, kind="group", body, optional transform
Repeat nodename, kind="repeat", body, count (integer or parameter name), step; optional head/tail and neighbor_links
Choice nodename, kind="choice", rule_id, probability (number or parameter), present/absent bodies
Explicit linkfrom, to, type
Random linkrule_id, from, to, pairing, probability, type
Network wrapperrandom_version=1, seed as decimal string, parameters, assembly

Use the complete crown assembly, PEG definition, and polyisoprene network as exact schema examples. They are serialized by the same Java builders shown in the tutorials, then loaded back during verification. This avoids guessing field names for advanced recipes.

Every structure operation

Every structure operation
opFieldsEffect
translateby: [x,y,z]Move all atoms
scaleby: number or [x,y,z]Scale coordinates
rotateaxis: [x,y,z], degreesRotate around the authored axis
affinematrix: 3 × 4 arrayApply an authored affine matrix
repeatcounts: 1–3 integers; optional wrap booleansExpand a unit cell; wrapping closes selected periodic boundaries
instancestransforms: matrix array; optional prefixPlace explicit copies and qualify names
appendstructure; optional instanceAppend a fragment, optionally with qualified names
editedits: edit-operation arrayApply the same editing contract as top-level edits
wrapCylindercircumference, axis, length; optional originWrap authored geometry without optimizing its chemistry

Operations execute in array order. A cell uses vectors and relative links; include a repeat operation to materialize it before returning a molecule structure. All coordinates must be finite. See the builder-serialized downloads for complete runnable recipes.
